verses.1: To the auspicious words of the righteous, blameless hermitess Hanuman replied:
verses.2: 'You are a righteous lady. You have given us refuge. Now in moving about the cave we have exceeded the time limit given by Sugriva.'
verses.3: Therefore you ought to deliver us—who at Sugriva's command overstepped our time and have lost our lives—out of this dreadful cave.
verses.4: 'O righteous lady we have a great task waiting. We are afraid of Sugriva as we could not accomplish our objective by staying here. Save us.'
verses.5: 'O righteous lady we have a great task waiting. We are afraid of Sugriva as we could not accomplish our objective by staying here. Save us.'
verses.6: To the words of Hanuman the ascetic replied, 'I consider it difficult for any one who enters here to go back alive.'
verses.7: 'I will help all monkeys out of this cave by virtue of my power of asceticism duly practised.
verses.8: Close your eyes, all you great monkeys, for it is not possible to get out with eyes unclosed.
verses.9: Happy at the prospect of getting out (of the cave) they all not only closed their eyes but also covered them with their delicate fingers.
verses.10: Then the great monkeys, faces covered with their hands, emerged from the cave in a moment.
verses.11: The righteous hermitess released all the monkeys out of that difficult situation and said these words of consolation:
verses.12: 'This Vindhya mountain has a rich collection of trees and bushes. This is Prasravana hill and this is the great ocean.O monkeys. Good luck to you. (Now) I am going back home'. Having said so, Svayamprabha entered the splendid cave.
verses.13: 'This Vindhya mountain has a rich collection of trees and bushes. This is Prasravana hill and this is the great ocean.O monkeys. Good luck to you. (Now) I am going back home'. Having said so, Svayamprabha entered the splendid cave.
verses.14: Then the monkeys saw the boundless, dreary ocean roaring wild with its terrific waves spread all over.
verses.15: While they were ransacking the impassable mountain created with the magical powers of Maya, the time limit of one month set by the king was over.
verses.16: Then the highsoul monkeys reached the hill adjacent to Vindhya mountain on which trees were in full bloom.They sat there, lost in thought.
verses.17: Alarmed at the thought (of transgression of time limit), the monkeys kept looking at the tree tops entwined with a hundred oreepers heavily loaded with the flowers of spring.
verses.18: Having realised (looking at the flowers) that spring has set in and they have exceeded the time limit, they all fell down on the ground.
verses.19: Coming to a conclusion after due deliberation Angada, heir apparent, profoundly wise, endowed with sturdy and broad shoulders like those of a lion or a bull, spoke in a sweet voice to the elderly, respectable monkeys, dwellers of the forest:
verses.20: Coming to a conclusion after due deliberation Angada, heir apparent, profoundly wise, endowed with sturdy and broad shoulders like those of a lion or a bull, spoke in a sweet voice to the elderly, respectable monkeys, dwellers of the forest:
verses.21: 'O monkeys don't you realize that all of us have come here at the command of the monkey king, and while we were in the cave a whole month has gone by?
verses.22: 'We started our journey in the month of Ashvayuja with a certain time limit. That has exceeded. What is the future course of action?
verses.23: You all are trusted and expert in the ways of policy, devoted to your master's welfare, and sent forth on every task with instructions.
verses.24: 'You are all celebrated for bravery and incomparable in your activities. You have followed me in obedience to the orders of the tawnyeyed Sugriva.
verses.25: 'We should be killed since we have failed to achieve the objective (of finding Sita). There is no doubt about it. Who can live in peace without executing the orders of the king?
verses.26: 'Now that the time limit fixed by Sugriva has expired, the right thing to do for the monkeys is to fast unto death.
verses.27: 'By nature Sugriva is harsh, and being a king now, he will not forgive us who are real offenders and have not done the task assigned.
